newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian lev's slide hits Bourgas refinery.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian lev's slide hits Bourgas refinery.

text.p: Bulgaria's biggest oil refinery Neftohim has suffered huge losses because of the recent slide in the lev, the refinery's executive director said.
Stefan Nedelchev told state television, "The current crude prices were based on a rate of 260 levs per dollar while the Neftohim refinery is buying it at almost double the price on the market."
"The refinery can still pay for the crude supplies but it will not be for long," he added.
Late on Monday the government unexpectedly announced a further rise in petrol prices by an average 21 percent and diesel prices by 26 percent.

The lev traded at 515-530 per dollar on the interbank foreign exchange market on Tuesday, compared to 355 on November 28 when petrol prices were increased by an average 9-10 percent and diesel by 8.7 percent.
The government usually revises energy prices each month in line with inflation, the exchange rate and world oil prices.
On November 28 the cabinet raised petrol and diesel prices for the second time in a month after the lev fell sharply against the dollar.
Since the end of November Bulgaria has been suffering from petrol and diesel shortages as suppliers hold back products in the expectation of price rises, energy officials have said.
Nedelchev said stockpiling by fuel distributors and traders was causing shortages in some towns.
Officials said the refinery would reduce the volume of Russian crude it was buying as the plant owed millions of dollars to some of its crude suppliers.
Nedelchev said the refinery had worked at lower capacity at the end of November due to difficulties in crude transportation across Russia to Russian Black Sea ports.
Supplies are regular now and a 70,000-tonne tanker is being unloaded at the Bourgas port, Nedelchev said.
Another tanker is waiting to be loaded with crude for Neftohim at Novorossiisk, he added.
Neftohim now produces 20,000 tonnes of petrol per day from 18,000 tonnes at the beginning of December, officials said. The plant's daily volumes were about 22,000 tonnes during the summer.
The refinery has now 152,000 tonnes of crude in storage, Nedelchev said.
